nationalOverlay.grain: SEC IARD roster firm with principal-office region = MN
nationalOverlay.label: SEC/IARD roster firms with a Minnesota principal office
nationalOverlay.caveat: A Minnesota principal office is not Minnesota state IA registration and is not a notice filing. These firms already exist in the federal graph.

stateRia.label: IAPD Minnesota state investment-adviser firms (APPROVED)
stateRia.caveat: Minnesota state IA registration is not SEC registration, not a federal notice filing, not ERA, and not a principal office. TERMREQUEST rows are reported separately; verify current status on IAPD. APPROVED is the IAPD status text, not an endorsement.

stateEra.statute: Minn. Stat. 80A.58 provides exemptions from investment-adviser registration
stateEra.label: Minnesota exempt reporting adviser (ERA) firms
stateEra.caveat: An exempt reporting adviser is not a Minnesota-registered IA and not an SEC RIA.

federalNotice.statute: Minn. Stat. 80A.60 (federal covered investment adviser notice filing)
federalNotice.acceptedFeedNote: The accepted IA_FIRM_SEC_Feed_09_17_2026 is no longer served by IAPD; the 2026-09-18 feed (SHA-256 recorded in the census) carries this lens on its own clock, as in NV-INV-001.

enforcement.capabilityBasis: Minn. Stat. 80A.79 (investigations and subpoenas) and 80A.81 (administrative enforcement)
enforcement.source: Minnesota Department of Commerce — CARDS (Commerce Actions and Regulatory Documents Search)
enforcement.access: Plain HTTP client: 403. Normal Chrome session: served, no challenge. One search; rendered table read. No download, no bypass.
enforcement.distinctCaseNumbersNote: CARDS prints a document number per row, not a case or matter number; unique matters are UNKNOWN.
enforcement.coverageNote: Commerce's CARDS index for the Securities industry type, signed 2022-01-01 through the retrieval date. One row per CARDS document; a row is not a unique matter (companion orders against a firm and its principals are separate rows).
enforcement.procedural: Action types are kept exactly as Commerce lists them. A consent order is a negotiated settlement and is not by itself an adjudicated finding.
